problem: A store manager is choosing $3$ employees to do the morning, afternoon, and night shifts. If the store has $9$ employees and each can work a single shift, how many ways of choosing the $3$ employees does the manager have?
worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $9$ employees to choose from, so $n=9.$ We want to select $3$ of them for the three different shifts, so we have $r=3.$ 

Therefore, the number of different choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{9}{P}_{3} & =\frac{9!}{(9-3)!} \\  & =\frac{9!}{6!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot \cancel{6!}}{\cancel{6!}} \\  & =9\cdot 8\cdot 7 \\  & =504.\end{aligned}
$$
